papers.title: Some complete $\omega$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $\Sigma^\omega$ in $\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k$, and by $\checked{D}_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $\Sigma$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $\omega$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\in\Sigma^\omega\mid\forall i\in\omega ~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $\checked{D}\_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0\_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k>3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $\omega$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $\checked{D}_{2n}(\mathbf{\Pi}^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbf{\Delta}^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

papers.title: Hamel-based TVG Stronger than the Usual Topology on R
papers.abstract: For every nonzero rational-valued additive functional on the real line, we construct a Hausdorff nondiscrete topological vector group topology strictly finer than the usual topology. We prove that two such topologies coincide exactly when their coefficient functionals differ by a nonzero real rescaling; every other pair is incomparable. The family contains as many distinct topologies as there are subsets of the real line. Their supremum is still nondiscrete and strictly finer than every individual member. We also prove failure of first countability and existence of maximal nondiscrete extensions.

papers.title: On condensations of $C_p(X)$ spaces onto Banach spaces with the weak topology
papers.abstract: We show that for a broad class of spaces $X$, the space $C_p(X)$ of continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the pointwise topology maps bijectively onto any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space with the weak topology. We prove that the inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ of any continuous bijection $\varphi: C_p(X)\to (E,w)$, where $X$ is an arbitrary infinite Tychonoff space and $(E,w)$ is an arbitrary normed space with the weak topology, is everywhere discontinuous. This generalizes a recent result of Kania--K\k{a}kol and solves a problem raised by K\k{a}kol, Leiderman and Michalak by providing a complete classification of function spaces $C_p(X)$ that are homeomorphic to Banach spaces with the weak topology.

papers.title: Locally convex spaces with hemicompact weak* dual
papers.abstract: For a locally convex space $L$ let $L'_\sigma$ denote its dual endowed with the weak* topology $\sigma(L',L)$. We prove that $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $L$ with the Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable and barrelled, and if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is $\sigma$-compact and quasi-complete. The key step is that a hemicompact $L'_\sigma$ is quasi-complete. The Mackey topology $\tau(L,L')$ is metrizable if and only if $L'$ is a countable union of absolutely convex weak*-compact sets; spaces with normable barrelled Mackey topology are characterized similarly. As a consequence, a metrizable (in particular, normed) space $L$ is barrelled if and only if $L'_\sigma$ is hemicompact. For function spaces we obtain: $(C_k(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is hemicompact, and $(C_p(X))'_\sigma$ is hemicompact if and only if $X$ is countable and all compact subsets of $X$ are finite.

papers.title: Probabilistic Powerdomains of Pointed FS-Domains are FS-Domains
papers.abstract: The Jung-Tix problem concerns the compatibility of probabilistic powerdomains with Cartesian closed categories of domains. We prove that both the subprobability and probability valuation powerdomains of every pointed FS-domain are FS-domains.

papers.title: A counterexample to Reich's fixed point problem
papers.abstract: This note provides a negative answer to the well-known Reich's problem in fixed point theory.

papers.title: Goldbach and Alexandroff Shake Hands
papers.abstract: We introduce a relational Alexandroff topology associated with the strong Goldbach conjecture on the set of even integers greater than or equal to six. The construction is induced by a multivalued map encoding Goldbach representations and leads naturally to a notion of relational reachability. For arbitrary binary relations, we show that singleton closures coincide with reachable sets and that the common intersection of all singleton closures consists exactly of the globally reachable points. In the Goldbach setting, this yields a topological characterization of the conjecture in terms of the distinguished point \(6\). In particular, the strong Goldbach conjecture is equivalent to the associated relational space being non-\(wR_0\) and connected. We also obtain compactness and supercompactness criteria in terms of the set of possible Goldbach exceptions.

papers.title: An Extension of Galvin's Theorem Related to the Banach-Mazur Game
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a topological space. Galvin's theorem on the Banach-Mazur game states that if $X$ has a $\pi$-base $\mathcal{B}$ satisfying the following condition: \textit{For any $U \in \mathcal{B}$, there exists a disjoint family $\mathcal{A}_U$ of nonempty open subsets of $U$ such that} \[ |\mathcal{A}_U| \geq |\{ B \in \mathcal{B} : U \subseteq B \}|, \] then, in the Banach-Mazur game on $X$, the second player, denoted NONEMPTY, has a 2-tactic if NONEMPTY has a winning strategy in this game. In this paper, we extend the disjointness condition of this family by replacing it with the condition of being open finite family. With this extension of the family $\mathcal{A}_U$, we showed that, the theorem is also true.

papers.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.

papers.title: Biquandle-Based Invariants of Virtual Knotoids and Connected Sum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the behavior of biquandle-based invariants of virtual knotoids under their connected sum. We first show that the fundamental biquandle of the connected sum of two virtual knotoids is the pushout of a span in the category of biquandles. By applying the Hom functor to this pushout description, we obtain the correspondence between biquandle colorings of $K_1 \# K_2$ and compatible pairs of colorings of summands. This provides a categorical explanation of a known matrix product formula for biquandle counting matrices under connected sum. We then study the behavior of biquandle virtual bracket invariants under connected sum. We introduce normalized multiset invariants derived from biquandle virtual brackets and show that they are strictly stronger than their unnormalized versions in certain cases by an explicit example. Furthermore, we show that for each coloring of the connected sum $K_1 \# K_2$ corresponding to a compatible pair of colorings of the summands $K_1$ and $K_2$, the normalized biquandle virtual bracket value factors as the product of the normalized values of the summands. Building on this, we obtain connected-sum formulas for the normalized multiset invariants defined by utilizing biquandle virtual brackets. When the coefficient ring is a number ring, the normalized bracket multisets can be encoded by polynomials and matrices with polynomial entries. We introduce an induced matrix product $\odot$ and show that the normalized biquandle virtual bracket matrices satisfy \begin{equation} \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1 \# K_2) = \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_1) \odot \widetilde{M}_X^\beta(K_2). \end{equation}

papers.title: Nielsen coincidence theory of $(n,m)$-valued pairs of maps
papers.abstract: We consider pairs of maps $(f,g)$, where $f$ is an $n$-valued map and $g$ is an $m$-valued map, defined on connected finite polyhedra. A point $x$ such that $f(x)\cap g(x)\neq \emptyset$ is called a coincidence point of $f$ and $g$. A useful device for studying coincidence points would be a Nielsen-type invariant which provides a lower bound for the number of coincidence points of all $(n, m)$-valued pairs of maps homotopic to $(f,g)$. The construction of such an invariant $N(f:g)$ was proposed in [J. Fixed Point Theory Appl. 14, 309--324 (2013)]. Unfortunately, this approach has some flaws. In this paper, we present a modified construction that yields a corrected form of the invariant, defined in terms of the intersection points of the graphs of $f$ and $g$. In the case of $(n, m)$-valued pairs of maps of the circle our invariant provides a sharp lower bound, which we precisely determine.

papers.title: Bounded uniform homeomorphisms between $C_p^*$-spaces preserve pseudocompactness
papers.abstract: For any Tychonoff space $X$ let $C_p(X)$ (resp., $C^*_p(X)$) be the set of all continuous (resp., and bounded) functions on $X$ with the pointwise convergence topology. Given Tychonoff spaces $X$ and $Y$, Uspenskij \cite{us} proved that if $C_p(X)$ is uniformly homeomorphic to $C_p(Y)$, then $X$ is pseudocompact if and only if $Y$ is pseudocompact. The second author and Vuma \cite{valvu} have shown that linear homeomorphisms between $C_p^*(X)$ and $C_p^*(Y)$ also preserve pseudocompactness. Recently Baars-van Mill-Tkachuk \cite{bmt} gave another proof of that result and raised the question if the same remains true provided $C_p^*(X)$ and $C_p^*(Y)$ are uniformly homeomorphic. In the present paper we introduce the notion of bounded uniformly continuous maps and show that every bounded uniform homeomorphism between $C_p^*(X)$ and $C_p^*(Y)$ preserve pseudocompactness. Moreover, we show that if there is a uniform homeomorphism $\varphi:C_p^*(X)\to C_p^*(Y)$, where $X$ is pseudocompact and $Y$ is normal, then $Y$ is $\sigma$-pseudocompact, i.e. $Y$ is a countable union of closed pseudocompact subsets. It is also shown that a continuous linear map between $C_p$-spaces is norm-bounded if and only if it is bounded in our sense.

papers.title: Separable quotients of pointwise function spaces and relative consistency
papers.abstract: Assuming Jensen's diamond principle, we construct a separable crowded compact zero-dimensional space $K$ of weight $\aleph_1$ and cardinality $2^{\aleph_1}$ such that $C_p(K)$ has no infinite-dimensional Hausdorff separable linear quotient. In particular, $K$ is an Efimov space: it contains neither a nontrivial convergent sequence nor a copy of $\beta\mathbb N$. We also prove in ZFC that the existence of a separable quotient of this kind is equivalent to the existence of a metrisable one. On the positive side, established finite-support random-sign methods give a split quotient of $C_p(K)$ onto $(c_0)_p$ whenever $K$ is infinite compact and $w(K)<\operatorname{cov}\mathcal N$, with explicit norm-one operators. Consequently, the universal quotient assertion for compacta of weight $\aleph_1$ is independent relative to the consistency of ZFC alone. A real-valued measurable continuum gives the positive result below the continuum and reduces the remaining problem to separable compacta of weight exactly the continuum. The counterexample uses direct diamond prediction, a simultaneous successor lemma, and a compactness argument converting localised measure limits into differences of point masses.

papers.title: Nullhomotopic equivariant shifts and Borsuk-Ulam-compatible compact abelian groups
papers.abstract: We disprove the classical version of the Borsuk-Ulam-flavored conjecture, due to Baum-D{\k{a}}browski-Hajac, that free actions $X\times \mathbb{G}\to X$ on non-empty compact Hausdorff spaces by non-trivial compact groups admit no equivariant maps $X*\mathbb{G}\to X$. Specifically, among non-trivial compact abelian $\mathbb{G}$, the conjecture fails precisely when $\mathbb{G}$ is torsion-free profinite.
